findings.text: The old escaping of ESC to  was removed. Any ESC not part of an SGR sequence matching ESC[digits;m, such as ESC[K, ESC[2J or a lone ESC, now goes into the XML raw. Raw control character 0x1B is illegal in XML 1.0, so JUnit parsers reject the report.

raw:
Issues: Other control char ESC not followed by color sequence is no longer escaped, leaving raw ESC (invalid XML 1.0). Also BASH_REMATCH[0] used as a glob pattern in replacement: `[` in it is a glob bracket, so `\033[31m` is parsed as a pattern with bracket expression `[31m]`, which matches one char instead of the literal sequence. That can cause an infinite loop: the pattern wouldn't match the literal text, so output never changes and the loop never ends.

Trace: the match is ESC[31m. The pattern ESC[31m, unquoted in the expansion, is read as ESC followed by a bracket expression, but there's no closing `]`, so `[` is literal. Bash treats an unmatched `[` as literal, so ESC[31m matches. Codes like `ESC[1;31m` also have no `]`. So it works in practice. The `+` in an ERE is fine. The remaining defect is raw ESC left behind.
